We need to determine number of CH3 groups in the sample's compound. We have no direct description of the sample. We need to infer from NMR? Probably we need to get 1H NMR spectrum and count methyl signals. Use proton_nmr_spectra tool (no input needed? It says takes SMILES string? Actually function signature: proton_nmr_spectra = (_: {}) => any. No parameters. So it will return the 1H NMR for the sample at hand (the unknown compound). Then we can analyze peaks: methyl groups appear as singlet (or doublet etc) around 0.9-1.5 ppm, integration of 3H each. But the tool returns a string with peaks and maybe integration? Not sure format. Could also use carbon_nmr_spectra to see number of methyl carbons (~10-30 ppm). But easier: carbon NMR: methyl carbons appear around 10-30 ppm. Count distinct signals in that region.

We need to minimize actions. Probably just get carbon NMR and count signals in 10-30 ppm region. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool.

Let's call carbon_nmr_spectra.
